title: Finishing in Canva: Layouts, Resizing and Text

The yoga studio image is generated by the team in advance: an empty studio with morning light, no people. The studio logo in the demo is a simple placeholder text mark made by the team for Arjun's fictional studio, not a real logo. The yoga mat image for Part B is generated, with no brand marks.
The hex codes on the slides (#0B5C8A, #1F6F5C) are shown, not read aloud.
Use a demo Canva account with no personal data visible. Blur account names and email addresses.
Arjun and his Pune yoga studio are fictional.

Hook.voiceover: Ask an image generator to write summer sale, twenty percent off, and you may get something like this. AI images are often great backgrounds, but they are not finished designs. The last step happens in a design tool.

Explain.voiceover: Image generators are good at pictures, but often weak at exact text, logos and precise brand colours. They can misspell words, invent letters or change a logo's shape.

slide.title: Finishing in Canva: Layouts, Resizing and Text
slide.body: AI Image Generation and Visual Design · Lesson 8 of 12 · Screen demo. A generated poster with broken, misspelled lettering, circled.

Explain.voiceover: So professional workflows follow one simple rule. Generate the picture with AI. Add real text, logos and exact colours in a design tool.
Explain.on_screen_text: Picture with AI, text in design

Explain.voiceover: Canva is a free design tool that works well for this. Four finishing tasks matter most. First, place your image in a layout of the right size. Second, add text in your brand fonts and colours. You enter your exact brand colour as a code in the colour picker, and design tools follow that code exactly, unlike most generators.

slide.title: Four finishing tasks
slide.body: 1. Place the image in a layout or template · 2. Add text in brand fonts and colours: hex code in the colour picker, e.g. #0B5C8A · 3. Remove backgrounds · 4. Resize for each platform

Explain.voiceover: Third, remove backgrounds to cut out a product. In Canva this may be a paid feature, and Firefly also offers options, so check your plan. Fourth, resize for different platforms, like a square post, a tall story and a wide banner. Automatic resize may need a paid plan. On the free plan, you create a new design and copy your elements into it.

slide.title: Check what your plan includes
slide.body: Background removal: Canva (may be paid) · Firefly and other tools (free options). Resizing: automatic resize (may be paid) · free plan: new design in the new size, copy the elements in.

Explain.voiceover: An AI image is like a freshly baked cake. It may taste excellent, but it is not ready for the party until someone adds the writing, the candles and the right plate. Canva is the decorating table.
One safety note. Do not upload confidential client files or photos of people without consent, and only use logos you own or have permission to use.

Demonstrate.voiceover: Let's help Arjun, who runs a yoga studio in Pune, India. He has a calm AI image of an empty studio with morning light, and he wants a social post for a new class. I open Canva, click create a design, and choose a square social post size.
screen_steps: Open Canva and sign in with a free account
Click Create a design
Choose a square social post size, or enter custom dimensions of 1080 × 1080 pixels

Demonstrate.voiceover: I upload the AI image in the uploads panel, drag it onto the page, and resize it to fill the page. Then I add a text box and type the headline. Sunrise Flow, Mondays at seven in the morning.
screen_steps: Upload the AI image using the uploads panel
Drag it onto the page and resize it to fill the page
Add a text box
Type the headline: 'Sunrise Flow – Mondays 7 am'

Demonstrate.voiceover: I choose a clear font. In the colour picker, I type the brand colour code you see on screen. Then I place the headline in the empty space, so it does not cover the main subject. Last, I place a small studio logo in a corner.
screen_steps: Choose a clear font
Open the colour picker and type the brand hex code #1F6F5C
Move the headline into the empty space of the image, away from the main subject
Upload the placeholder studio logo and place it small in a corner
Demonstrate.on_screen_text: Exact brand colour: type the code

Demonstrate.voiceover: Now an optional step. I select a yoga mat image, open the edit image options, and find the background remover. Notice whether it is marked as a paid feature on your plan.
screen_steps: Select a product image, such as a yoga mat
Open the edit image options
Find the background remover
Point out whether it is marked as a paid feature

Demonstrate.voiceover: Next, resizing. On a paid plan, the resize option creates copies in the story size and a wide banner size. On the free plan, I create a new design in the story size, then copy and paste the image, headline and logo into it.
screen_steps: On a paid plan: use the resize option to create copies at 1080 × 1920 (story) and a wide banner size
On the free plan: create a new design at the story size
Copy and paste the image, headline and logo into it

Demonstrate.voiceover: In each new size, I move the headline so it stays clear and readable. In the tall story, I move it higher. In the wide banner, I move it to the side. Then I download each design as a PNG file.
screen_steps: In the story, move the headline higher
In the banner, move the headline to the side
Check that the headline is clear and readable in each size
Download each design as PNG

Demonstrate.voiceover: The most common mistake is to accept an automatic resize without checking it. Text can end up over the subject, or the logo can fall off the edge. Always review each size by eye. And do not ask the generator for text. Leave that space empty and add text in Canva.

Recap.voiceover: Let's recap. First, generate the picture with AI, then add real text, logos and exact brand colours in a design tool such as Canva. Second, background removal and automatic resizing are useful, but which features are free changes often, so check your plan. Third, review every resized version by eye, because text and subjects can move to the wrong place.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Picture with AI; text, logos and exact colours in Canva. 2. Free features change: check your plan. 3. Review every resized version by eye.

CTA.voiceover: Now it is your turn. In the exercise below, you will place one of your images in a Canva social post with a headline in your brand colours, then create a story and a banner version. It takes about twenty-five minutes. In the next lesson, we learn about spotting and fixing common flaws. See you there.
